name: Stratum Corporate Services Polo
description:
Stratum issues this polo to client-facing staff across its service subsidiaries — lobby attendants, corporate hospitality coordinators, guest relations personnel, and lower-tier administrative support who interact with the public. The fabric is a tight-knit polycotton in Stratum's proprietary charcoal-and-white color palette, with the Stratum logotype embroidered in white thread at the left chest. The collar is a standard two-button polo cut, stiff enough to stay presentable through an eight-hour shift, and the fit is designed to look neat across a range of body types without tailoring.

Off the clock, Stratum employees are technically prohibited from wearing issued uniforms in public — a policy nobody enforces and nobody follows. In Tier 2 neighborhoods near Stratum transit hubs and logistics centers, these polos are everywhere. Some people buy the knockoff version from street vendors who've copied the colorway without the embroidery. The shirt itself is perfectly comfortable. It's just that wearing it always reads as 'I work for someone.'
materials: moisture-wicking inner panel at back yoke
what_it_says: You're in the system. You represent something larger than yourself, and you've made a kind of peace with that.
worn_by: people who haven't changed after their shift
story_hooks: A Stratum polo in perfect condition found on the Shelf — no ID tag, no employee number, no explanation for how it got there.
Someone wearing a knockoff Stratum polo is waved through a corporate checkpoint by a guard who doesn't look closely enough at the embroidery.
A Stratum employee discovers their issued polo has a serial number stitched into the hem — and that number is associated with a different employee who was terminated six months ago.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A crisp, corporate-casual polo that reads 'functional employee' at a glance. The charcoal base with white geometric striping creates a subtly authoritative silhouette — not intimidating, but unmistakably uniform. On the street, it signals middle-management precarity: steady employment within a mega-corp ecosystem, but visible labor.
physical_description.fit: Straight-cut and slightly tapered through the torso. Designed for comfort across diverse body types without custom tailoring — roomy enough at the shoulders, not billowing at the waist. The sleeves hit mid-bicep with a clean seam. Intended to look 'neat' rather than fashionable; it achieves this through precision fit rather than style.
physical_description.primary_material: Proprietary polycotton blend — likely 65% polyester, 35% cotton. Tight-knit weave that resists wrinkles and maintains shape through heavy wear. Machine-washable, fade-resistant, designed for institutional laundry cycles.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and uniform to the touch, with a subtle sheen from the synthetic content. No visible texture variation — the fabric is engineered for consistency. The collar has reinforced stitching that keeps it stiff and symmetrical.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray base (approximately Pantone 18-0605) with thin white vertical pinstripes at irregular intervals, creating visual rhythm without drawing attention. The Stratum logotype is embroidered in white thread at the left chest — minimalist, sans-serif, corporate-standard.
physical_description.closures: Standard two-button polo collar with button-through placket. The buttons are resin (matte gray) — functional, not decorative. No additional closures; the fit is designed to sit naturally without fastening.
distinctive_features: White-thread Stratum logotype embroidery on left chest — subtle but unmistakable identifier
Proprietary charcoal-and-white colorway that's become iconic in Tier 2 transit zones
Reinforced collar stitching designed to withstand frequent wear and institutional washing
Slightly oversized fit through the torso to accommodate diverse body types without tailoring
Pocket-free design — eliminates bulk and maintains clean lines
Uniform weave consistency that resists visible wear patterns despite heavy use
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 corporate uniform. Signals stable, corpo-affiliated employment but not executive status. The standardization and mass production are visible in its perfect uniformity.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this on-shift = client-facing Stratum subsidiary employee (hospitality, guest relations, administrative support). Wearing it off-shift in Tier 2 neighborhoods = either a rule-breaker comfortable with their visible corporate affiliation, or someone buying credibility through a knockoff. In Tier 3-4 zones, it can read as either 'I have a job' or 'I'm pretending to have legitimacy.'
physical_description.condition_typical: When new: pristine, crisp collar, bright white embroidery. After regular wear: still functional and neat, but the white stripes may yellow slightly from washings, the collar softens, and the embroidery thread can fray at the edges. Knockoff versions deteriorate faster — their imitation embroidery lifts within weeks.
